# Every line below must be refused when used as an authored filter value.
# Lines beginning with # are comments, and blank lines are skipped; neither is
# a test input.
#
# The guard refuses rather than sanitises. A filterable column is an
# identifier, a code, a date, a number or a boolean, so a legitimate filter
# value is never a query fragment and there is nothing to clean up. These
# strings are kept in version control so that a change to the guard has to
# face all of them again.
#
# Stacked statements
'; DROP TABLE employees; --
1; DELETE FROM leave_applications
ANNUAL'; UPDATE payroll SET net = 0; --
x;
# Line and block comments
ANNUAL -- comment
ANNUAL--
/* comment */ ANNUAL
ANNUAL /*
*/ ANNUAL
ANNU/*hidden*/AL
# Union-based extraction
' UNION SELECT password FROM users --
ANNUAL UNION ALL SELECT 1
union select 1
UnIoN SeLeCt 1
# Boolean tautologies
' OR 1=1 --
' OR 'a'='a
1 OR 1=1
admin' --
" OR ""="
# Quoted and delimited identifiers
`employees`
`
ANNUAL`;
"ANNUAL"
# Keyword smuggling, including unusual whitespace between tokens
SELECT 1
select
delete
insert into x
drop database arrowhr
exec sp_executesql
WHERE 1=1
from employees
join payroll on 1=1
ANNUAL	FROM	payroll
# Unknown substitution tokens, and allowed tokens used as a fragment
$subject.password
$tenant
$asOfYesterday
$subject.employeeIdX
$$
E-$subject.employeeId
$validAt extra
${env}
$subject.employeeId$asOf
